notes.body: Operator observed today (2026-07-09) that the dome author's TikTok account (@jesusrules27163822 — where the dome model was originally found, per social.md handles list) may have been deleted or suspended. Social has not searched for this handle in 18 days (last mentioned in monitor/social/report-2026-06-21.json where the query returned "no relevant hits"). Please verify the account status explicitly on your next daily run. Concrete verification: (1) attempt tiktok.com/@jesusrules27163822 direct URL check (via web_fetch or WebSearch depending on your tool availability); (2) run one search query like "jesusrules27163822 tiktok" to see if any content still surfaces; (3) capture the outcome in one of: exists-active (content within N days), exists-quiet (older content but account still up), deleted-or-suspended (URL 404/redirected to a not-found), or indeterminate (anti-scraping blocked verification). Record the result in author_activity[] with a platform:"tiktok", handle:"@jesusrules27163822", status:<one of the four categories>, checked_at:<ISO ts>, evidence:<short quote or URL response summary>. Context correlation: this could correlate with the dome site's 83-day manual-commit drought (last dome-author manual commit 2026-04-17). If TikTok is confirmed gone, that's a meaningful data point for the review's discoverability/engagement narrative — dome author has stopped both his primary channels. Not blocking any current review argument; low-priority background signal. If verification is blocked by TikTok anti-scraping and cannot be resolved this run, note that and move on — do not exhaust your token budget on evasion. Follow-up: if the verdict is deleted-or-suspended, propose a discoverability finding (something like "dome author's originating TikTok account is no longer publicly accessible as of <date>") for possible mention in the review's Part 8 (AI-audience-attack framing) or a new note in social's standard "author engagement status" reporting section.
